basis: Hand-set from one Mac M4 (the heavy GPU scene in 0.8 ms) and one software renderer (67 ms). CPU re-based at v0.1a: the kernel now flies the 6-DOF Kestrel hands-off, crashes and respawns included, which runs at 0.41 of the v0.0b spectator kernel on the same machine (WASM single under Node on the M4: 137 000 against 333 000 ticks per second), so the three CPU thresholds were scaled by 0.41 and every machine keeps its tier. To be tuned against the reference-machine reports (OQ-01, AC-60.6). Re-based again at v0.1c (ADR-28, amendment 1) for the kernel changes since v0.1a (the control system, the gear and physiology, v0.1b): the three CPU thresholds were scaled by 0.420, the ratio of the current benchmark kernel to the v0.1a tag's, measured alternately under Node (WASM single, the benchmark kernel's own procedure; `packages/tools/src/kernel-rate.ts`) on the M4: 56 934 against 135 436 ticks per second (two rounds of three 10 s runs each per build). The two browser reports on the same M4 give 58 177 / 148 828 = 0.391, 7 % apart (inside the 10 % allowance); the Node ratio is the one used. The M4 reads High again. Thresholds before this re-base: 41000 / 74000 / 107000.

cpu.unit: kernel ticks per second on one thread, higher is better

gpuHeavyMs.unit: milliseconds per frame with 64 patches at 1080p, lower is better

gpuPresetMs.unit: milliseconds per frame with 64 patches at 1080p: the slowest each preset may be

memoryGb.unit: navigator.deviceMemory, which browsers round and cap (8 in the specification; headless Chrome 156 reported 16): memory can fail a machine but cannot rank it above Minimum
